metadata.methods_description: MEG and EEG data were recorded from 30 participants as they viewed 21,600 video clips spanning 180 categories of human action, using the same participants and stimuli as the previously released HAD-fMRI dataset.

citation_details.title: Autopoietic Cycles in Encephalography: Model Validation on Open Data
citation_details.author: Sergei Surnin
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: This paper presents an empirical validation of the ontological model of autopoietic cycles, previously developed in the author's theoretical work, using non‑invasive neuroimaging methods — magnetoencephalography (MEG) and scalp electroencephalography (EEG). The model introduces formal concepts: the stable internal model D, its changes ∇D, the self‑reference threshold C′, and the perception operator κin. Based on open MEG data (ds007353, n=30; COGITATE, subject CA124) and EEG data (ds002718, n=18; ds005429, n=15), we propose operational projections of these concepts adapted for non‑invasive methods: κin is defined as the correlation between early (0.3–0.5 s) and sustained (0.5–0.7 s) gamma‑band activity (30–50 Hz) in the prefrontal and posterior cortex, respectively; D as stable categorical clustering in the posterior cortex using representational similarity analysis (RSA); C′ as the ROC‑derived threshold distinguishing target from standard stimuli in an oddball paradigm. The results confirm the model’s predictions. The perception operator κin exhibits an invariant negative sign: in the MEG dataset ds007353, all 30 subjects (100%) showed negative correlation (mean –0.082 ± 0.038); in the COGITATE MEG data (subject CA124) κin reached –0.584; in EEG, all 33 subjects (100%) from two independent datasets showed negative values (means –0.402 ± 0.067 and –0.413 ± 0.070, respectively). The stable internal model D, estimated from the EEG dataset ds002718, reveals significant categorical clustering in the posterior cortex (mean RDM = 0.486 ± 0.058), with the largest distance between the categories “famous faces” and “scrambled faces” (0.806 ± 0.220). The self‑reference threshold C′ in the EEG dataset ds005429 is close to zero (C′ ≈ 0), with AUC = 0.505 ± 0.017, replicating results previously obtained from invasive recordings. These findings demonstrate that all three components of the autopoietic cycle model can be reliably measured using non‑invasive MEG and EEG data, opening avenues for applying the proposed ontological framework in consciousness and cognitive research.

citation_details.title: Autopoietic cycles in encephalography: testing the predictions of the structure on open data
citation_details.author: Sergei Surnin
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: The paper proposes an empirical test of the structure of autopoietic cycles, previously developed in the author‘s theoretical works, using data from non‑invasive recording methods — magnetoencephalography (MEG) and scalp electroencephalography (EEG). The structure includes the following elements: a stable internal model D, its changes ∇D, a self‑reference threshold C′, and a perception operator κin. Based on open MEG data (ds007353, n=30; COGITATE, subject CA124) and EEG data (ds002718, n=18; ds005429, n=15), operational correspondences of these elements adapted for non‑invasive methods are proposed: κin is associated with the correlation between early (0.3–0.5 s) and sustained (0.5–0.7 s) gamma activity (30–50 Hz) in the prefrontal and posterior cortex, respectively; D is associated with stable categorical clustering in the posterior cortex (RSA); C′ is associated with ROC analysis of the threshold for discriminating target and standard stimuli in an oddball paradigm. The results confirm the predictions derived from the structure of autopoietic cycles. The operator κ_in exhibits an invariant negative sign: in the MEG dataset ds007353, all 30 subjects (100%) showed a negative correlation (mean –0.082 ± 0.038); in the COGITATE MEG data (subject CA124), the value of κin reached –0.584; in the EEG data, all 33 subjects (100%) from two independent samples (means –0.402 ± 0.067 and –0.413 ± 0.070, respectively) also showed a negative sign. The stable internal model D, estimated from the EEG dataset ds002718, reveals significant categorical clustering in the posterior cortex (mean RDM = 0.486 ± 0.058), with the largest distance between the categories “famous faces” and “scrambled” (0.806 ± 0.220). The self‑reference threshold C′ in the EEG dataset ds005429 is close to zero (C′ ≈ 0), AUC = 0.505 ± 0.017, reproducing the results previously obtained with invasive recordings. Additionally, wavelet analysis was used to estimate gamma coherence between the prefrontal and posterior cortex (0.552 ± 0.072), which differs significantly between “famous faces” and “scrambled” (p = 0.0006) and correlates weakly with κin (r = –0.417), indicating the independence of these two characteristics. The obtained results demonstrate that the key elements of the structure of autopoietic cycles can be related to measurable empirical referents in non‑invasive MEG and EEG data, opening up prospects for applying the proposed structure in consciousness research and cognitive studies.
